√वच् (adādi, 2P ‘to speak’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, kartari prayoga

sandhi.note: Final ā before initial u: the two vowels fuse into o, and the words are written as one.

morph.note: Nominative singular of the n-stem राजन्: the final n is dropped and the vowel lengthened (राजन् → राजा).

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: Suratha answers the merchant Samādhi, who has just told him (1.21–25) how his wife and sons took his wealth and drove him out, and how he still worries about them. The two exiles have met in the forest near the sage Medhas’s hermitage (1.17).

words.g: relative pronoun यद्, m. instr. pl.; agent of the passive participle निरस्तः; correlative तेषु in 1.28
निर् + √अस् (divādi, 4P ‘to throw’) + क्त (past passive participle), m. nom. sg.; predicate of भवान्
m. nom. sg. of भवत्, the respectful pronoun of address (construed with the third person)
√लुभ् (divādi, 4P ‘to covet’) + क्त, used as an adjective, m. instr. pl.; qualifies पुत्रदारादिभिः

words.en: by sons, wife and the rest
words.g: m. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to यैः

words.en: lit. ‘by riches’; here ‘for the sake of wealth’
words.g: n. instr. pl. of धन; instrumental of cause (hetu)

sandhi.note: After a vowel other than a/ā, the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before a voiced consonant: यैः → यैर् before n. The same change gives पुत्रदारादिभिर्धनैः.

-aḥ before the voiced bh becomes -o. Then final n before l becomes a nasalised l: भवान् लुब्धैः → भवाँल्लुब्धैः. The Gita Press writes the nasal colour with candrabindu (ँ) on the vowel before the double l.

samasa.vigraha: पुत्राश्च दाराश्च पुत्रदाराः; पुत्रदाराः आदयः येषां ते, तैः
samasa.literal: those of whom sons and wife are the first
samasa.sense: sons, wife and the other members of the household

morph.note: Past passive participle of निर् + √अस् ‘throw’: ‘thrown out’. With the instrumental यैः it makes a passive clause: ‘by whom you were cast out’.
The polite ‘you’: nominative of भवत्, a pronoun that takes the verb in the third person. Its final n meets the l of लुब्धैः and becomes a nasalised l (भवाँल्लुब्धैः).
Instrumental of cause: ‘because of (your) wealth’. The plural is idiomatic for ‘riches’. See Uncertain.

mantras.anvaya: यैः लुब्धैः पुत्रदारादिभिः धनैः (हेतुभिः) भवान् निरस्तः, (तेषु …)
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause only: its correlative तेषु and the main verb come in the next half-verse (1.28).
mantras.lit: Those greedy ones — sons, wife and the rest — by whom you were cast out on account of wealth,
mantras.tr: Those greedy ones — your sons, your wife and the rest — who drove you out for the sake of your wealth:

comm.t: The king restates Samādhi’s own account (1.22: ‘cast out by sons and wife out of greed for wealth’). The question it leads to comes in the next half-verse.

Read with 1.12–14, the question is ironic: Suratha has just been worrying, in the same way, about the kingdom, servants and elephant that were taken from him. He asks the merchant what he cannot yet answer for himself; he admits as much in 1.41–45.

flags.uncertain: धनैः: the instrumental plural is read here as cause (‘on account of wealth’). Some translators take it loosely as ‘(deprived) of your wealth’, echoing 1.22 (पुत्रैरादाय मे धनम्). The reading itself is not in doubt.

words.g: pronoun तद्, m. loc. pl. (locative of the object of feeling); correlative of यैः in 1.27
indeclinable (interrogative adverb, the n. acc. of किम्)
m. gen. sg. of भवत् (respectful ‘you’); qualifies मानसम्
m. acc. sg. of स्नेह; object of अनुबध्नाति
अनु + √बन्ध् (kryādi, 9P ‘to bind’), laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
n. nom. sg. of मानस; subject of अनुबध्नाति

sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra.

sandhi.rule: मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) does not apply before a vowel
sandhi.note: Final m stays m before a vowel and is written together with the next word.

morph.note: Present of the ninth class: the root बन्ध् loses its nasal and takes the class sign ना (बध्ना-ति). With अनु: ‘to bind to, to attach’; स्नेहम् अनुबध्नाति ‘forms an attachment’.
Taddhita from मनस् ‘mind’: मानस ‘belonging to the mind’, used as a noun for the mind itself.

mantras.anvaya: भवतः मानसं तेषु स्नेहं किम् अनुबध्नाति?
mantras.anvaya_en: The main clause of the question begun in 1.27: subject मानसम्, object स्नेहम्, the locative तेषु for the persons loved.
mantras.lit: — why does your mind bind affection to them?
mantras.tr: why does your mind still hold to them in affection?
mantras.tr_note: ‘Still’ renders the force of the question in context; it is not a separate word.

comm.t: The king’s question: why love those who have wronged you? It is the question of the whole first carita, and the merchant will answer that he does not know (1.31–34).
A modern reading: the question is easier to ask of another than of oneself. The text lets the king hear his own trouble in a stranger’s voice before he can name it.

words.g: m. nom. sg. of वैश्य (a man of the vaiśya class, here a merchant); subject of उवाच
√वच् (adādi, 2P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, kartari prayoga

sandhi.note: As in 1.1: -aḥ before a vowel other than a becomes y, the y is dropped, and the two vowels stand apart.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: Samādhi replies to the king’s question (1.27–28).

words.g: indeclinable (adverb of manner); predicate of एतत्
demonstrative pronoun एतद्, n. nom. sg.; subject
indeclinable (relative adverb of manner)
प्र + आह; आह is the form substituted for √ब्रू (adādi, 2U ‘to speak’) in the present (laṭ), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada, with perfect-type endings
m. nom. sg. of भवत् (respectful ‘you’, with a third-person verb); subject of प्राह
n. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies वचः
n. acc. sg. of वचस् (s-stem); object of प्राह

sandhi.note: Final m stays m before the vowel e and is written joined; the final t of एतत् becomes d before the voiced y.

sandhi.rule: ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् (8.3.32) does not apply
sandhi.note: Final n is doubled before a vowel only after a short vowel; after the long ā of भवान् it simply joins the next word.
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

samasa.alt: Also glossed अस्मद्विषयकम् ‘having us as its subject’; the sense is the same. The plural stem अस्मद् is used of the one speaker, a usage the grammarians allow for the first person.

morph.note: आह looks like a perfect but is, for Pāṇini, a present: the first five present endings of √ब्रू are optionally replaced by perfect-type endings with आह for the root. With प्र: ‘says, declares’.
Nominative of भवत्, the pronoun of respect: ‘you’ in meaning, third person in grammar (प्राह, not a second-person form).

mantras.anvaya: भवान् अस्मद्गतं वचः यथा प्राह, एतत् एवम् (अस्ति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause of manner (यथा … प्राह) and a nominal main clause with the verb ‘is’ understood: एतत् एवम्.
mantras.lit: This is so, as you, sir, have spoken the words concerning me.
mantras.tr: It is just as you say about me.

comm.t: Samādhi grants the king’s point at once: those he loves have treated him cruelly. What follows (1.31–34) is not a defence of them but a confession that his mind will not obey what he knows.
